note: 25 -> 27 on 2026-08-28 for THREE declarations landing across three branches at once (Gabe, 2026-08-28: "give it the row and bump the ceiling to 27"). NOT a regression in any of the three: each is a NEW invariant where none existed, which is the case the +1s below already record. (1) ui/reserved-slot-out-of-the-card-floor (GIT_142): a reserved status slot's contribution to its card's min-content had no declaration at all — .color-clash was `flex: 0 0` with a 35u basis and nobody had written down that a slot which cannot shrink holds the row open at its full basis. Rung 4 because the mechanism with full coverage is a source assertion over app.css (test/intrinsic-floors.test.ts) that derives the slot set from the sheet's own mark rule, derives each slot's rendered class list from the TSX, and merges the plain-class-compound cascade; the promotion recorded on the declaration is the mirror of judgeFloor in dev/layoutAudit.ts swept over the whole registry in a real layout, which reads the resolved cascade from the browser and needs no selector vocabulary. (2) ui/field-input-growth-is-bounded (GIT_144): `.field input[type=text]` carried `flex: 1` and no ceiling, and there was no declaration saying a growable field must say where it stops. Rung 4 for the same reason — a source scan of app.css — with the promotion being declared per-content-kind classes plus a lint, which is Gabe's call because it changes the look of four cards. (3) The row GIT_136 was approved to add for its own new guard: a flex child with a fixed `height` and `overflow: hidden` has an automatic minimum size of zero, so it shrinks with the card and makes contentRowSpan a function of the card's own size (.shp-caveat was measuring 0px at its registry size). That mechanism is already written and already runs in the node suite; only its register row was deferred, and it was deferred FOR THIS EXACT REASON — the branch could not take the count past the then-ceiling of 25 without ruling on a number that was not its to rule on (see the @note on dev/layoutAudit.ts). It lands at rung 4, source-text analysis over app.css, promoting to one shared declaration every fixed-height clipped row extends. HEADROOM IS INTENDED, NOT AN OVERSHOOT. `uat` sits at 24; GIT_142 and GIT_144 each carry it to 25 on their own, and GIT_136's row is written on GIT_136 by whoever finishes that branch. So on any tree where only one or two of the three have landed, the gate passes with slack rather than exactly, and that is the point: the ceiling is raised ONCE, on both of the branches that need it, in identical bytes so git merges it without a conflict, instead of three branches each racing to move the same number. DO NOT tidy this back down to 25 or 26 on the grounds that the count is lower than the ceiling on the tree you are looking at — that breaks GIT_136 the moment its row merges, which is the failure this note exists to prevent. Lower it only when a declaration is actually PROMOTED, and say which. Previously: 24 -> 25 on 2026-08-26 for mock-duet/g28-axis-set-from-model (GIT_102). NOT a regression: G28's axis handling carried no @invariant at all before — it checked a hardcoded ["X","Y","Z"] against the code's letters with no declaration, so this is a NEW invariant where none existed, not a dropped rung on an existing one. It lands at rung 4 because the mechanism with full coverage today is a source-text scan (test/gcode-derivation.test.ts) that reads the G28 case's own text for a quoted axis letter; TypeScript offers no barrier against writing `letter === "X"` again because `Om` is `Record<string, any>` throughout this package, so `axis.letter` typechecks against any string literal. The promotion recorded on the declaration is a branded AxisLetter type mintable only from a lookup in om.move.axes; that needs the OM typing tightened first, which is bigger than this fix. It comes off when that lookup type lands and the source scan becomes structurally unnecessary. Previously: 23 -> 24 on 2026-08-25 for shaping/the-shaper-to-restore-is-read-once-per-run (GIT_84). NOT a regression: that invariant has existed since GIT_59, at the same rung 5, with the same mechanism. It was excluded from the count because its declaration carried no @debt and so failed validation outright — an invalid declaration is not counted as debt, it is not counted at all. Making it valid is what made it countable, so this +1 buys back a row the ratchet had been blind to rather than admitting a new one. It comes off when the run's prior gets its own branded type, minted once at run start and required by Procedure.plan, which is the promotion recorded on the declaration. Worth noting what this episode says about the ratchet itself: a malformed declaration HIDES debt from the gate that exists to count it, and six of them hid this one for six merges. Previously: 22 -> 23 on 2026-08-23 for connector/clock-seam (GIT_43), a NEW invariant rather than a regression: the connectors' timers had no declaration at all before, they were simply written against the platform. It lands at rung 4 because the mechanism with complete coverage is a source walk (test/clock-fence.test.ts); the compile-time `declare const setTimeout: never` shadow on top of it is rung 7 but only in the files that carry it. It comes back off when the platform timers are made unnameable package-wide, which is the promotion recorded on the declaration. Previously: 21 -> 22 on 2026-08-21 for ui/unit-lengths, re-rated 7 -> 4. Nothing regressed there either: the lint is exactly as strong as it was, but it is a node:test that `pnpm build` never runs and no CI or hook runs for anyone, so 'build-failing' overstated it. That +1 is that honesty, not new debt, and it comes off the moment `pnpm test` runs on the path to main.
